title: An AI boom is sending San Francisco rents through the roof: ‘Nowhere left for people to go’
key_facts: The average one-bedroom in San Francisco costs about $4,400, up more than 25% on last year.
San Francisco rent board figures show eviction notices up 44% citywide year on year.
Mayor Daniel Lurie declared a "rent emergency" in September, citing costs driven by the AI boom.
He proposed eviction legal aid, larger payments to displaced renters and caps on rent rises for newly vacant rent-controlled units.
Advocates say landlords use the Ellis Act, condo conversions and "renovictions" to clear tenants; properties sell for up to $1m over asking to AI-industry buyers.
The Housing Rights Committee clinic says it is at full capacity; repair disputes are up 23%.
quote_evidence: Today, the average one-bedroom in the city by the Bay costs $4,400, a figure that is up more than 25% from last year and that is nearly three times the national average.
Calculations by the San Francisco rent board show eviction notices are up 44% citywide compared with last year.
why_it_matters_hint: Tenants, including middle-income workers, are being priced or pushed out as AI wealth lifts housing costs.
notes: Rent figures and the link to the AI boom are the Guardian's reporting and advocates' views; one outlet.
